title: Identifying Treatment-Reordering Effects in Dynamic Fixed-Effect Logit Panels from Factual Histories
banked_reason: BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR — genuine subfield contribution, but insufficient reach for the required field tier; bank downgraded or rewind D-1.2.
gap_reasons: The result identifies only a selected-stratum contrast under known slopes and a constant auxiliary index; it does not identify population regime effects, unknown slopes, or time-varying-index schedules.

The design theorem is exact and non-obvious enough for a field contribution, but its practical reach is constrained by those maintained restrictions and by the absence of an applied exogenous-schedule demonstration or inference analysis.

The closest-literature discussion establishes a plausible distinction through a bounded search rather than a definitive priority comparison, limiting the projected leading-journal score despite the internally complete theorem package.
proof_attempt_summary: The run completed an exact all-horizon theory for selected positive-probability strata with known slopes, homogeneous indices, and equal-dose schedules, including an iff reduced-pole criterion, collision-complete valuation, constructive weights/twins, and a sharp minimum-panel-length elbow. The mathematics passed the panel review, but the cold tier gate capped the package at subfield because population effects, unknown slopes, and time-varying indices remain outside the architecture. A field-tier successor must re-anchor at D-1.2 around one of those broader targets rather than reopen this D0 proof.
tldr: Can factual outcome histories identify the selected-stratum causal effect of reordering the same number of treatments when every deterministic intervention follows one homogeneous dynamic fixed-effect logit, slopes are known, the auxiliary index is constant, and the conditional fixed-effect law is unrestricted? With potential outcomes \(Y^s\), consistency \(Y=Y^D\), and no assignment-ignorability premise, the proposal seeks an all-horizon answer: factor every equal-dose terminal contrast through a signed word-area polynomial, prove that two explicit curves and edge parity exhaust noncollision pole losses, and combine merged-root valuation with a minimal-likelihood denominator to obtain an exact identification test, constructive history weights, or strictly positive observational twins.
gap: General causal schedule notation, likelihood-weight, moment-space, and partial-fraction methods exist, but the inspected literature does not characterize how an arbitrary equal-dose intervention word determines the pole orders of its selected-stratum causal terminal contrast, does not classify the exceptional positive-parameter loci, and does not provide a merged-root if-and-only-if design test with positive common-support failure witnesses.
fill: Under the explicit potential-outcome transition model and consistency, prove the word factorization, injectivity and signed-edge lemmas; derive the two universal exceptional curves with one-order parity losses; establish full minimal-denominator likelihood span; and package the result as a finite all-parameter pole algorithm with constructive weights or positive twins.
